-- 10_rm: namespace, version, lifecycle, event wiring. -- Contract (docs/design.md): one global namespace `rmap`, nothing else leaks. -- Load/install (sysLoadEvent, sysInstall) runs rmap.start(), which runs the -- init functions other modules appended to rmap.inits (they build their -- temp triggers/aliases/UI). sysUninstallPackage runs rmap.stop(), which -- kills every registered handler/trigger/alias id. Every id a module -- creates must be tracked here via rmap.on / rmap.alias so teardown is total.
-- Re-running the script (Mudlet re-executes it on save): tear down first. local wasStarted = rmap and rmap.started if rmap and rmap.stop then rmap.stop() end rmap = {} rmap.restart = wasStarted rmap.name = "retromud-mapper" rmap.version = "0.0.27" rmap.inits = {} rmap.started = false rmap.mapping = false rmap.uiContract = 1
-- The one writer of rmap.mapping: tells the GUI when the flag changes. function rmap.setMapping(on) on = on and true or false if rmap.mapping == on then return end rmap.mapping = on raiseEvent("rmap.onMapping", on) end rmap.ids = { handler = {}, trigger = {}, alias = {} }
-- One tagged line per message: "[rmap] text". level colours the tag: -- "ok" green, "skip" yellow, "err" red, nil cyan, "plain" no tag, and -- "markup" no tag with the caller's own cecho colours (help body). -- Output can land on the prompt's line, so start a new line first -- when the last line already has text. -- getLines(from, to) excludes `to` (checked live), hence last + 1 local COLOR = { ok = "green", skip = "yellow", err = "red" } function rmap.out(text, level) local last = getLastLineNumber("main") local cur = getLines(last, last + 1)[1] if cur and cur ~= "" then echo("\n") end if level ~= "markup" then text = text:gsub("<", "<<") end if level == "plain" or level == "markup" then cecho(text .. "\n") else cecho("<" .. (COLOR[level] or "cyan") .. ">[rmap]<reset> " .. text .. "\n") end end
function rmap.on(event, fn) local id = registerAnonymousEventHandler(event, fn) rmap.ids.handler[#rmap.ids.handler + 1] = id return id end
function rmap.alias(pattern, fn) -- unverified: tempAlias accepts a Lua function as its code argument local id = tempAlias(pattern, fn) rmap.ids.alias[#rmap.ids.alias + 1] = id return id end
function rmap.start() if rmap.started then return end rmap.started = true for i = 1, #rmap.inits do rmap.inits[i]() end end
function rmap.stop() for i = 1, #rmap.ids.handler do killAnonymousEventHandler(rmap.ids.handler[i]) end for i = 1, #rmap.ids.trigger do killTrigger(rmap.ids.trigger[i]) end for i = 1, #rmap.ids.alias do killAlias(rmap.ids.alias[i]) end rmap.job = nil -- delete, not hide: a hidden pane stays registered under its name, and the -- next install then builds a second one while the GUI adopts the stale one if rmap.pane then pcall(rmap.pane.delete or rmap.pane.hide, rmap.pane) rmap.pane = nil end if rmap.ids.timer then killTimer(rmap.ids.timer) end -- the one documented global exception (see 60_speedwalk): put back the -- profile's own, but only if the global is still ours if doSpeedWalk == rmap.speedwalk then doSpeedWalk = rmap.prevSpeedWalk end rmap.prevSpeedWalk = nil rmap.ids = { handler = {}, trigger = {}, alias = {} } rmap.started = false end
rmap.on("sysLoadEvent", function() rmap.start() end) -- unverified: sysInstall is raised with (event, packageName) after an -- .mpackage install, and after this script body has already run rmap.on("sysInstall", function(_, pkg) if pkg == rmap.name then rmap.start() end end) rmap.on("sysUninstallPackage", function(_, pkg) if pkg == rmap.name then rmap.stop() end end)
-- 20_settings: defaults + merge/load/save of user overrides. -- Contract (docs/design.md): defaults in code, user overrides merged from -- a table.save'd file in the profile dir; per-character prompt/exits -- patterns; persisted UI geometry. No behavior. Phase 0 holds defaults -- only; persistence arrives with the first setting that needs it.
rmap.settings = { -- Fallback prompt pattern (Lua pattern), used when the connection -- sends no GA and by offline replay. Not end-anchored. See -- docs/output-format.md "Prompt patterns". -- Allows an "EQ Tick: " style prefix and a negative Sp. promptPattern = "^[%w ]*:? *Hp:%s*%d+/%d+%s+Sp:%s*%-?%d+/%d+%s+Ep:%s*%d+/%d+", -- The short tick prompt (nothing after Ep). It can land between a -- command and its output (swimming: "You are in deep water...", short -- prompt, then the room block), so once a full prompt has been seen a -- segment ending at it is "soft" and closes no command. shortPrompt = "^Hp:%s*%d+/%d+%s+Sp:%s*%-?%d+/%d+%s+Ep:%s*%d+/%d+%s*$",
-- Exits grammar (docs/output-format.md "Exits grammar"). The solo -- pattern is lazy so the trailing period is not captured. exitsMulti = "^Obvious exits are:%s+(.*)", exitsNone = "^There are no obvious exits%.?%s*$", exitsSolo = "^The only obvious exit is%s+(%S-)%.?%s*$",
-- Noise lines skipped when looking for the room title. ignore = { "^You are flying%.$", "^.- starts using ", "^ %*%*%* NEW ROUND %*%*%*", "^%-%-%- HP:", "^You hit ", "^You do not hit ", "^You attack ", " fails to hit you%.$", " hits you ", "is DEAD, R%.I%.P%.$", "^You can act again%.$", "^The clouds begin to break apart", },
-- Lines buffered with no prompt before reporting "no usable prompt". maxBlockLines = 500,
-- Seconds before an unresolved expectation is dropped (a silent or -- failed command must never stall the queue). expectTimeout = 10,
-- Command classification (docs/mapper-protocol.md). First word of -- the sent command; extend during calibration. verifyVerbs = { look = true, l = true, glance = true }, previewVerbs = { peer = true, scry = true }, -- Teleports that work from any room: they re-sync by fingerprint, never -- become a special exit (a "wizhome" link on every room walked from). -- Freeform verbs that mean "back the way you came in": from a room entered -- by another exit they lead back to it, even among look-alikes. leaveVerbs = { out = true, leave = true, exit = true, back = true }, teleportVerbs = { ["goto"] = true, wizhome = true, home = true },
-- Lines that cancel the head expectation (a move that did not move). moveFail = { "^You can't go that way!" },
-- Fold an exit onto a look-alike room that sits two cells from where it -- points (a non-Euclidean map). Off: in the areas walked it only ever -- merged different rooms that share a name and exits (forests, camps), -- and a duplicate is easy to merge by hand while a false merge breaks paths. nearMerge = false, -- Freeform verbs that are vertical in meaning: layers to climb (layout -- only; the link is by room id either way). freeformDz = { climb = 1 }, areaName = "RetroMUD",
-- Map zoom set when a guild seed loads (lower is closer). The default of 20 is too far out to -- read the room symbols; 8 shows about a dozen rooms in the map pane. Returning players keep theirs. seedZoom = 8,
-- Room blocks the game prints around character creation and the first -- login. They are not part of the world: capture never raises them, so -- neither the tracker nor the seeder sees them. By fingerprint. ignoreRooms = { ["Character Creation|enter,prev,shrines"] = true, ["Race Selection Room|next,prev"] = true, ["Guild Selection Room|next"] = true, ["Welcome to RetroMUD|enter,skip"] = true, -- one-time disclaimers room -- the creation shrines (stat boosts) off Character Creation: a hub and -- fourteen identical rooms ["A room full of shrines|agi,allstats,cha,con,dex,hermmax,int,maxsize,minsize,out,per,skillmax,spirmax,str,wis"] = true, ["A small shrine|out"] = true, },
-- Cardinal directions: abbreviation, Mudlet direction number -- (setExit/setExitStub), coordinate delta, opposite. in/out are not -- here: they have no delta, so they are freeform (special) exits. dirs = { north = { abbr = "n", num = 1, dx = 0, dy = 1, dz = 0, opp = "south" }, northeast = { abbr = "ne", num = 2, dx = 1, dy = 1, dz = 0, opp = "southwest" }, northwest = { abbr = "nw", num = 3, dx = -1, dy = 1, dz = 0, opp = "southeast" }, east = { abbr = "e", num = 4, dx = 1, dy = 0, dz = 0, opp = "west" }, west = { abbr = "w", num = 5, dx = -1, dy = 0, dz = 0, opp = "east" }, southeast = { abbr = "se", num = 7, dx = 1, dy = -1, dz = 0, opp = "northwest" }, southwest = { abbr = "sw", num = 8, dx = -1, dy = -1, dz = 0, opp = "northeast" }, south = { abbr = "s", num = 6, dx = 0, dy = -1, dz = 0, opp = "north" }, up = { abbr = "u", num = 9, dx = 0, dy = 0, dz = 1, opp = "down" }, down = { abbr = "d", num = 10, dx = 0, dy = 0, dz = -1, opp = "up" }, }, }
-- 30_capture: line buffer -> room-block detection -> rmap.onRoom event. -- Contract (docs/design.md, docs/output-format.md): rmap.onLine(line) is -- called once per received line (a trigger live, the replay harness -- offline). Segments end at a prompt: isPrompt() (GA/EOR) live, else -- rmap.settings.promptPattern. Each exits line in a segment raises -- raiseEvent("rmap.onRoom", {name=, exits={...}, lines={...}, -- fingerprint=}), then rmap.onSegment(n); a move-fail line raises -- rmap.onMoveFail. Knows nothing about the map.
rmap.cap = { buf = {}, warned = false }
local function isNoise(line) if line:find("^%s*$") then return true end for i = 1, #rmap.settings.ignore do if line:find(rmap.settings.ignore[i]) then return true end end return false end
-- Exits starting at buf[i]: returns exits list, index of last line. local function parseExits(buf, i) local s = rmap.settings if buf[i]:find(s.exitsNone) then return {}, i end local solo = buf[i]:match(s.exitsSolo) if solo then return { solo:lower() }, i end local rest = buf[i]:match(s.exitsMulti) if not rest then return nil end local j = i while not rest:find("%.%s*$") do j = j + 1 if not buf[j] then return nil end if not isNoise(buf[j]) then rest = rest .. " " .. buf[j] end end local exits = {} -- names never contain spaces (underscores), so "a and b" splits too for name in rest:gsub("%.%s*$", ""):gmatch("[^,%s]+") do if name ~= "and" then exits[#exits + 1] = name:lower() end end return exits, j end
local function fingerprint(name, exits) local sorted = {} for i = 1, #exits do sorted[i] = exits[i] end table.sort(sorted) return name .. "|" .. table.concat(sorted, ",") end
-- A plausible title: not a continuation (lowercase start) and not a -- list header ("There are several special commands here:"). local function titleLike(line) return not line:find("^%l") and not line:find(":%s*$") and not line:find("^[^%w\"'(]") end
-- Nearest non-noise, non-indented line above d, or nil. local function titleAbove(buf, lo, d) local t = d - 1 while t >= lo and (isNoise(buf[t]) or buf[t]:find("^%s")) do t = t - 1 end if t >= lo then return t end end
-- Walk back from each exits line to a description start: a line indented -- 2 spaces, else 3+ (builders vary: 2, 4, 10; deeper indents inside a -- description are boxes and lists, so exactly 2 wins) whose non-noise, non-indented -- predecessor looks like a title. A later paragraph's first line has a -- sentence fragment above it, so nearer candidates with such a -- predecessor are skipped. Description-less rooms (title, then the -- single-space light line) fall back to that light line. local function findTitle(buf, lo, i) for _, pat in ipairs({ "^ %S", "^ $", "^ +%S", "^ +$", "^ %S" }) do for d = i - 1, lo, -1 do if buf[d]:find(pat) then local t = titleAbove(buf, lo, d) if t and titleLike(buf[t]) then return t end end end end end
-- Last resort for areas whose descriptions are not indented at all: the -- earliest line before the exits line that reads as a title (short, not -- indented, no sentence punctuation at the end) and is directly followed -- by text. Chatter ends in punctuation ("...tower.'", "...alarm!"). local function bareTitle(buf, lo, i) for t = lo, i - 2 do local l = buf[t] if not isNoise(l) and not l:find("^%s") and #l <= 60 and not l:find("[%.!?'\"%]%)]%s*$") and titleLike(l) and not isNoise(buf[t + 1]) then return t end end end
-- Returns the index after the last exits line handled. local function scan(buf) local lo, i = 1, 1 while i <= #buf do local exits, last = parseExits(buf, i) if exits then local t = findTitle(buf, lo, i) or bareTitle(buf, lo, i) if t then local lines = {} for k = t, last do lines[#lines + 1] = buf[k] end local name = buf[t]:match("^(.-)%s*$") local fp = fingerprint(name, exits) if not rmap.settings.ignoreRooms[fp] then raiseEvent("rmap.onRoom", { name = name, exits = exits, lines = lines, fingerprint = fp, }) end end lo, i = last + 1, last + 1 else i = i + 1 end end return lo end
-- Raises rmap.onRoom per room, then rmap.onSegment(n, soft) with the count of -- non-noise lines, so the tracker can close commands that print no room. -- keepTail: on a forced flush keep the unscanned tail so a room whose -- title is already buffered is not split from its exits line. -- soft: the segment ended at a short tick prompt, so it may be only the -- first half of a command's reply (see settings.shortPrompt). local function flush(keepTail, soft) local buf = rmap.cap.buf rmap.cap.buf = {} local lo = scan(buf) if keepTail then for k = math.max(lo, #buf - 40), #buf do rmap.cap.buf[#rmap.cap.buf + 1] = buf[k] end end local n = 0 for i = 1, #buf do if not isNoise(buf[i]) then n = n + 1 end end raiseEvent("rmap.onSegment", n, soft) end
function rmap.onLine(line) local c = rmap.cap if isPrompt() or line:find(rmap.settings.promptPattern) then c.warned = false local soft = false if line:find(rmap.settings.shortPrompt) then soft = c.tall -- a tick prompt, not a reply else c.tall = true end flush(false, soft) return end -- a reconnect banner (login art) is never part of a room if line:find("^%% Connected to") then c.buf = {} end for i = 1, #rmap.settings.moveFail do if line:find(rmap.settings.moveFail[i]) then raiseEvent("rmap.onMoveFail") break end end c.buf[#c.buf + 1] = line if #c.buf > rmap.settings.maxBlockLines then if not c.warned then c.warned = true rmap.out("no usable prompt (no GA, and the prompt " .. "pattern never matched in " .. #c.buf .. " lines); " .. "set rmap.settings.promptPattern", "err") end flush(true) end end
rmap.inits[#rmap.inits + 1] = function() -- unverified: tempRegexTrigger("^", fn) fires for every line, and -- the global `line` holds the current line inside fn local id = tempRegexTrigger("^", function() rmap.onLine(line) end) rmap.ids.trigger[#rmap.ids.trigger + 1] = id end
-- 40_tracker: expectation queue and sync state. -- Contract (docs/design.md, docs/mapper-protocol.md): sysDataSendRequest -- pushes one classified expectation (VERIFY / PREVIEW / ADVANCE / -- MAYBE_MOVE) per sent command; sync state is SYNCED / UNSYNCED / -- PENDING; each rmap.onRoom block resolves the queue head. Decides -- advance/verify/preview. Never writes the graph (rmap.build does). -- Rules 3 and 4 of the protocol hold by construction: T.send below is -- the only function that pushes onto the queue; no module calls -- sendSocket or pushes directly.
rmap.track = { q = {}, pos = nil, handled = false, following = false } local T = rmap.track
-- name or abbreviation -> full direction name local dirAlias = {} for name, d in pairs(rmap.settings.dirs) do dirAlias[name] = name dirAlias[d.abbr] = name end
function rmap.now() return os.time() end
local function classify(cmd) local word = cmd:match("^(%S+)") if rmap.settings.verifyVerbs[word] then return "VERIFY" end if rmap.settings.previewVerbs[word] then return "PREVIEW" end if rmap.settings.teleportVerbs[word] then return "TELEPORT" end if dirAlias[cmd] then return "ADVANCE", dirAlias[cmd] end return "MAYBE_MOVE" end
-- An expectation can carry cb(block_or_nil, why): called when it -- resolves (block), is cancelled (nil, "fail"), closed with no room -- (nil) or expires (nil, "timeout"). Used by speedwalk/scan/where. local function done(e, b, why) if e and e.cb then e.cb(b, why) end end
-- room id, name and area name of the current position (nil when UNSYNCED) function T.where() if not T.pos then return end local ok, name, area = pcall(function() return getRoomName(T.pos), getRoomAreaName(getRoomArea(T.pos)) end) if ok then return T.pos, name, area end return T.pos end
-- Tell the GUI when the sync state or the position changed since last time. function T.notify() local st = T.state() if st ~= T.lastState then T.lastState = st raiseEvent("rmap.onState", st) end if T.pos and T.pos ~= T.lastPos then raiseEvent("rmap.onMoved", T.where()) end T.lastPos = T.pos end
local function expire() local cutoff = rmap.now() - rmap.settings.expectTimeout local dead = {} while T.q[1] and T.q[1].t < cutoff do local e = table.remove(T.q, 1) dead[#dead + 1] = e -- a step we never saw land leaves us unsure where we are; a late -- reply must not be linked from the old room (it re-syncs by -- unique fingerprint instead). Only directions: an unrecognised -- verb that printed nothing ("get gold") is not a lost move. if e.kind == "ADVANCE" then T.pos = nil end end for i = 1, #dead do done(dead[i], nil, "timeout") end if #dead > 0 then T.notify() end end
-- SYNCED / PENDING / UNSYNCED (PENDING = synced with a command in flight) function T.state() if not T.pos then return "UNSYNCED" end if #T.q > 0 then return "PENDING" end return "SYNCED" end
-- Rule 1 and 2: skip empty commands, one expectation per embedded line. function T.send(_, cmd) for raw in (tostring(cmd) .. "\n"):gmatch("(.-)\r?\n") do local part = raw:lower():match("^%s*(.-)%s*$") if part ~= "" then -- the player moved on mid-job: later steps/previews would come -- from another room, so the job stops here (its callbacks -- see rmap.job == nil and drop out) if not T.hook and rmap.job then rmap.out(rmap.job .. ": stopped, you sent a command", "skip") rmap.job = nil end expire() local kind, dir = classify(part) T.q[#T.q + 1] = { kind = kind, cmd = part, dir = dir, t = rmap.now(), cb = T.hook } T.hook = nil -- unverified: `follow` syntax; "follow self"/"unfollow" end it local verb, arg = part:match("^(%S+)%s*(%S*)") if verb == "follow" then T.following = arg ~= "" and arg ~= "self" elseif verb == "unfollow" then T.following = false end end end T.notify() end
-- Internal sends (speedwalk, scan, where) go through send() so that -- T.send above still pushes the expectation; cb rides on it. function T.exec(cmd, cb) T.hook = cb -- unverified: sysDataSendRequest handlers run synchronously in send() send(cmd) -- no expectation took the callback (not connected, no event): end the -- job now, or it would wait forever and block every later job local lost = T.hook T.hook = nil if lost then return lost(nil, "not sent") end -- a silent game must not stall a job: expire() runs from this timer if rmap.ids.timer then killTimer(rmap.ids.timer) end -- unverified: tempTimer(seconds, fn) returns a timer id for killTimer rmap.ids.timer = tempTimer(rmap.settings.expectTimeout + 1, expire) end
local function resolve(e, b) if e.kind == "PREVIEW" then return end if e.kind == "TELEPORT" then T.pos = rmap.build.find(b.fingerprint) -- known room or lost, never a link return end local cur = T.pos -- mapping off: follow what is already mapped, never write the graph local move = rmap.mapping and rmap.build or { advance = rmap.build.follow, special = rmap.build.follow } if not cur then -- never guess: only a unique fingerprint match re-syncs T.pos = rmap.build.find(b.fingerprint) elseif e.kind == "ADVANCE" then T.pos = move.advance(cur, e.dir, b) elseif e.kind == "MAYBE_MOVE" and rmap.build.known(cur, e.cmd, b) then T.pos = rmap.build.known(cur, e.cmd, b) -- into a look-alike room elseif rmap.build.fp(cur) == b.fingerprint then -- VERIFY / no move return elseif e.kind == "VERIFY" then T.pos = rmap.build.find(b.fingerprint) else T.pos = move.special(cur, e.cmd, b) end end
-- Keep the Mudlet map pane on the player's room (it follows the area). -- unverified: centerview(id) switches the pane to that room's area. function T.focus() if T.pos then centerview(T.pos) end end
local function onRoom(_, b) expire() T.handled = true local e = table.remove(T.q, 1) if not e then -- SPONTANEOUS -- The game printing the room we are already in (after registration, -- say) is not movement. Any other room means we may have been moved -- (drag, summon, or a lost position healing): sync only to the one -- known room with this fingerprint, never guess, never create. Twin -- rooms share a fingerprint, so a forced move between twins goes -- unnoticed. (pcall: the position may name a room deleted since.) local same = T.pos and select(2, pcall(rmap.build.fp, T.pos)) == b.fingerprint if not same then T.pos = rmap.build.find(b.fingerprint) T.focus() end return end resolve(e, b) T.focus() done(e, b) end
function T.onRoom(...) onRoom(...) T.notify() end
-- A failed move cancels the head expectation; nothing was created on send. function T.onMoveFail() expire() T.handled = true local e = table.remove(T.q, 1) if e and e.kind == "ADVANCE" and T.pos and rmap.mapping then rmap.build.reject(T.pos, e.dir) end done(e, nil, "fail") T.notify() end
-- A prompt closed a segment with n real lines. If no room block and no -- fail message already resolved the head, the head command is done. -- An ADVANCE head is the exception: its ack is the room block or the -- fail line, so unrelated chatter before it must not close it (timeout -- covers a move that prints neither). A soft segment (ended by a short -- tick prompt) closes nothing: swimming prints "You are in deep water..." -- and a short prompt before the room block. function T.onSegment(_, n, soft) expire() local e, head = nil, T.q[1] if not T.handled and not soft and n > 0 and head and head.kind ~= "ADVANCE" then e = table.remove(T.q, 1) end T.handled = false done(e, nil) end
-- Explicit orphan creation / re-sync entry point (used by `rmap where`). function T.adopt(b) T.pos = rmap.build.adopt(b) T.focus() T.notify() end
rmap.inits[#rmap.inits + 1] = function() rmap.on("sysDataSendRequest", T.send) rmap.on("rmap.onRoom", T.onRoom) rmap.on("rmap.onMoveFail", T.onMoveFail) rmap.on("rmap.onSegment", T.onSegment) end
-- 45_seed: put every guild map into the player's map, and welcome a new player. -- Contract: build.py embeds each seeds/<guild>.json as rmap.seedData. Whenever the -- package starts, and again at the first room block of a session, every seed the -- map has not yet had is merged in as its own area (named for the guild). Merging adds -- rooms with fresh ids and never touches or replaces a room the player already has -- (loadJsonMap replaces the whole map, so it is not used). Which seeds were merged is -- kept in the map's user data, so a deleted area is not brought back. -- A new character is told apart by an empty map at the first merge: that sets -- "rmap.welcome" to pending, and the first room block then puts the player on their -- room (a guild start room is in the map), turns mapping on, opens the map pane and -- zooms in. Everyone else just resumes mapping, unless they ran `rmap stop`. -- Runs after 40_tracker so the tracker has already resolved the block (a spontaneous -- login block leaves T.pos nil). Creation and first-login rooms never reach it: -- see settings.ignoreRooms.
rmap.seed = { checked = false } local S = rmap.seed
-- The player's explicit `rmap start` / `rmap stop` is kept in the map's user -- data, so it survives sessions and goes with the map. Unset means "on". S.PREF = "rmap.mapping" function S.remember(choice) setMapUserData(S.PREF, choice) end function S.wantsMapping() return getMapUserData(S.PREF) ~= "off" end
S.MERGED, S.WELCOME = "rmap.merged", "rmap.welcome"
-- Mudlet direction numbers (the same as settings.dirs) local DIRNUM = { north = 1, northeast = 2, northwest = 3, east = 4, west = 5, south = 6, southeast = 7, southwest = 8, up = 9, down = 10, ["in"] = 11, out = 12 }
local function names(csv) local t = {} for n in (csv or ""):gmatch("[^,]+") do t[n] = true end return t end
-- One seed as a new area. Returns the number of rooms added. function S.mergeSeed(name, d) if getAreaTable()[d.area] then return 0 end -- the player already has an area of that name local area = addAreaName(d.area) if not area then return 0 end local ids, made = {}, {} for _, r in ipairs(d.rooms) do local id = createRoomID() addRoom(id) setRoomArea(id, area) setRoomName(id, r[2]) setRoomCoordinates(id, r[3], r[4], r[5]) for k, v in pairs(r[8]) do setRoomUserData(id, k, v) end ids[r[1]], made[#made + 1] = id, id end for _, r in ipairs(d.rooms) do local from = ids[r[1]] for dir, to in pairs(r[6]) do if ids[to] then if DIRNUM[dir] then setExit(from, ids[to], DIRNUM[dir]) else addSpecialExit(from, ids[to], dir) end -- a named exit, e.g. "college" end end for _, dir in ipairs(r[7]) do setExitStub(from, DIRNUM[dir], true) end end rmap.icons.apply(name, made) return #made end
-- Merge every seed the map has not had. A new character's map is empty: mark it. function S.mergeAll() local done = names(getMapUserData(S.MERGED)) local todo = {} for name in pairs(rmap.seedData or {}) do if not done[name] then todo[#todo + 1] = name end end if #todo == 0 then return 0 end table.sort(todo) local fresh = next(getRooms() or {}) == nil and next(done) == nil local n = 0 for _, name in ipairs(todo) do n = n + S.mergeSeed(name, rmap.seedData[name]) done[name] = true end local list = {} for name in pairs(done) do list[#list + 1] = name end table.sort(list) setMapUserData(S.MERGED, table.concat(list, ",")) if fresh then setMapUserData(S.WELCOME, "pending") end if updateMap then updateMap() end return n end
function S.onRoom(_, b) if S.checked then return end S.checked = true -- once per session, whatever happens -- Whatever is still queued comes from commands typed before this room -- (creation, login, registration): none can relate to the map. local function finish(msg, cb, ok) rmap.job = nil T.focus() if msg then rmap.out(msg, ok and "ok" or "skip") end if cb then cb(ok) end end
-- Neighbour of room `id` through exit `ex` (linked or special), or nil. local function beyond(id, ex) return getRoomExits(id)[ex] or getSpecialExitsSwap(id)[ex] end
-- Peer each exit of `b` and drop candidate rooms whose known neighbour -- through that exit has another fingerprint. Calls done(room or nil). local function narrow(c, b, i, id, done) if #c <= 1 then return done(c[1]) end local ex = b.exits[i] if not ex then return done(nil) end T.exec("peer " .. ex, function(pb) if not live(id) then return end -- cancelled if pb then local keep = {} for _, id in ipairs(c) do local n = beyond(id, ex) if not n or B.fp(n) == pb.fingerprint then keep[#keep + 1] = id end end c = keep end narrow(c, b, i + 1, id, done) end) end
-- rmap where: look; unique fingerprint -> synced; several -> disambiguate -- by peering; none -> report (or adopt when mapping). cb(ok) when done. local function where(cb) local id = rmap.jobId T.exec("look", function(b) if not live(id) then return end -- cancelled if not b then return finish("where: no room seen", cb, false) end local c = B.candidates(b.fingerprint) if #c == 1 then T.pos = c[1] return finish("where: synced", cb, true) end if #c == 0 then if not rmap.mapping then return finish("where: no match in the map", cb, false) end T.adopt(b) return finish("where: created a new room", cb, true) end narrow(c, b, 1, id, function(room) if not room then return finish("where: could not narrow to one room", cb, false) end T.pos = room finish("where: synced", cb, true) end) end) end
function rmap.commands.where() if not rmap.canRun() then return end startJob("where") where() end
-- rmap scan: peer every exit that is not already linked to a real room. function rmap.commands.scan() if not rmap.canRun() then return end if not rmap.mapping then return rmap.out("scan writes rooms: type 'rmap start' first", "skip") end local id = startJob("scan") local function scan() T.exec("look", function(b) if not live(id) then return end -- cancelled local cur = T.pos if not b or not cur or B.fp(cur) ~= b.fingerprint then return finish("scan: position lost", nil) end -- cardinals first: freeform rooms take the nearest free cell -- and must not squat on a cardinal neighbour's cell local order = {} for _, want in ipairs({ true, false }) do for _, ex in ipairs(b.exits) do if (rmap.settings.dirs[ex] ~= nil) == want then order[#order + 1] = ex end end end local made, i = 0, 0 local function nextExit() i = i + 1 local ex = order[i] if not ex then return finish("scan: done, " .. made .. " new", nil, true) end local to = beyond(cur, ex) if to and getRoomUserData(to, "source") ~= "peer" then return nextExit() end T.exec("peer " .. ex, function(pb) if not live(id) then return end -- cancelled if not rmap.mapping or T.pos ~= cur then return finish("scan: stopped", nil) end if pb then local n = #B.created if rmap.settings.dirs[ex] then B.advance(cur, ex, pb, true) else B.special(cur, ex, pb, true) end made = made + #B.created - n end nextExit() end) end nextExit() end) end if T.state() ~= "UNSYNCED" then return scan() end where(function(ok) -- where() already ended the shared job; only a newer job voids this if rmap.jobId ~= id then return end if not ok then return finish("scan: could not sync", nil) end rmap.job = "scan" scan() end) end

"' (room " .. e.id .. ")", "ok") return true end
